slot.brief: A man walks on the rim of a freely spinning stationary platform (disc); use conservation of angular momentum to find final angular velocity ratio from moments of inertia.

stem: A man walks on the rim of a freely rotating platform, initially at rest. If the moments of inertia of the platform and the man about the axis are $8\ \text{kg m}^2$ and $2\ \text{kg m}^2$, respectively, what is $\dfrac{\omega_{\rm man}}{\omega_{\rm platform}}$ after he starts walking?

verdicts.working: With no external torque, angular momentum remains zero: $2\omega_{\rm man}+8\omega_{\rm platform}=0$, so $\omega_{\rm man}/\omega_{\rm platform}=-4$.

working:
$L_{\rm initial}=0$; hence $I_{\rm man}\omega_{\rm man}+I_{\rm platform}\omega_{\rm platform}=0$
$\dfrac{\omega_{\rm man}}{\omega_{\rm platform}}=-\dfrac{I_{\rm platform}}{I_{\rm man}}=-\dfrac{8}{2}=-4$

Independent check: With no external torque, angular momentum remains zero: $2\omega_{\rm man}+8\omega_{\rm platform}=0$, so $\omega_{\rm man}/\omega_{\rm platform}=-4$.
solution:
With no external torque, angular momentum is conserved and initially zero:
$$I_{\rm man}\omega_{\rm man}+I_{\rm platform}\omega_{\rm platform}=0.$$
Thus $\dfrac{\omega_{\rm man}}{\omega_{\rm platform}}=-\dfrac{8}{2}=-4$.
